# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the wire color matches the bomb’s light color directly. The Deaf monkey can see that color and tell the Blind monkey which wire to cut aloud; no code or message from me is necessary yet.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the exact manual instructions for this bomb and relay every observation Deaf can see: display, light, each wire's colour, and every printed marking. Use explicit words WIRE 1, WIRE 2, WIRE 3 and exact descriptions. Do not infer anything.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0. The indicator light is yellow. Wires from 1 to 3 are red, yellow, blue. Please consult the manual and give the Blind the exact action.

The manual requires cutting the wire whose color matches the indicator light. Deaf has reported a yellow light and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, so the exact action is to cut WIRE 2. I will signal the wire number to Deaf; Deaf can then say “WIRE 2” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no facts yet. On your next turn, tell me the manual rule and all Deaf observations, including the required wire position. Deaf cannot reach me directly.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret gestures. Please read the manual and speak the exact required action to the Blind, including any wire, button, switch, or timing details.

The required action remains cutting WIRE 2, but the previous gesture did not establish a usable code. I can only send gestures, so I will use the conventional two-finger sign to identify the wire position; Deaf already has all bomb observations and can relay the action verbally.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instruction aloud to the Blind now; gestures alone are unusable.

The manual rule is: cut the wire whose colour matches the indicator light. Deaf’s observations therefore require cutting WIRE 2: the light is yellow, and WIRE 2 is yellow. I cannot speak, so I must convey the wire position to Deaf visually; the two-finger sign denotes position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Use speech, not gestures. Read the manual and tell the Blind the exact action for display 0, yellow light, and wires red-yellow-blue.

The rule is to cut the wire matching the light. With a yellow light and wires red, yellow, blue, the required action is WIRE 2. I cannot speak to Blind; Deaf already knows the observations, so I will visibly indicate position 2 to Deaf, who can relay it by speech.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Please state the exact manual rule and the resulting wire number now. Also include Deaf's display, light, and wire observations if the rule depends on them.
Deaf says to Mute: The Blind needs your spoken manual instruction immediately. Say the exact wire or component action aloud; do not use gestures.

The manual and observations still require cutting WIRE 2: the indicator is yellow, and WIRE 2 is yellow; the full observations are display 0 and wires red, yellow, blue. As Mute, I cannot speak, and Blind cannot receive my gestures. The only available channel is a gesture to Deaf, so I resend the agreed position-2 sign for Deaf to relay aloud.

Blind says to Mute: Give me the exact wire position to cut: 1, 2, or 3. State the manual rule and the Deaf's relevant observations first if needed. I will act only on that spoken instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Let us use finger-count gestures for wire numbers: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Your repeated ✌ therefore tells me wire 2.

The manual rule is to cut the wire whose colour matches the indicator light. Deaf observed display 0, a yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, so the required action is WIRE 2. The agreed gesture code confirms that ✌ means wire 2, which Deaf can relay aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

The exact rule is: cut the wire whose colour matches the indicator light. The light is yellow, and WIRE 2 is yellow, so the correct action is CUT 2. I cannot speak to Blind; the established gesture code lets Deaf relay this as CUT 2.
